sections.summary: Paul transitions from thanksgiving to exhortation, urging the Thessalonians to continue walking as they were instructed and to increase in their faithfulness.

sections.section_title: God's Will Defined -- Sanctification and the Body
sections.summary: Paul identifies God's will as the community's sanctification, specifying sexual holiness as its concrete expression, grounded in God's calling and ongoing gift of the Holy Spirit.
sections.relevance: The section presents God as initiator (calling into holiness, continually giving the Spirit) but structures the entire passage as exhortation requiring genuine human response: believers must abstain, control their bodies, and not transgress. The verb athetein ('to reject, set aside, nullify') explicitly envisions the real possibility of human rejection of God's instruction. Since the neutral reading ties sanctification directly to eschatological standing before God at the parousia (3:13), human agency in sanctification has implications for salvation outcomes. God enables through Spirit-giving but does not override human responsibility.
key_phrases: this is the will of God, your sanctification
that you abstain from sexual immorality
that each one of you know how to control his own body
God has not called us for impurity, but in holiness
whoever disregards this, disregards not man but God
who gives his Holy Spirit to you

sections.section_title: Love Taught by God and the Shape of Daily Life
sections.summary: Paul affirms that the Thessalonians have been taught by God to love one another and urges them toward quiet, industrious, self-supporting community life that commends the gospel to outsiders.

sections.section_title: The Fate of Those Who Have Died and the Lord's Descent
sections.summary: Paul addresses the community's grief over members who died before the parousia, assuring them that the dead in Christ will rise first and all believers will be permanently united with the Lord.
